title: Cards and rarity
summary: In TCG Card Shop Simulator every card is an object with a rarity, a price and a look, and the game keeps those as separate pieces of information you interact with at your counter.
body: Cards exist as physical objects you handle, and the same card can be displayed, priced and sold.
Rarity is a defined set of levels rather than a free number, and the game has a screen where a rarity is chosen.

A card's own record carries more than its name. It holds the border the card is printed with, its grade, and flags for whether it is foil, whether it is a champion card and whether it is new, which is why two copies of the same card can differ in what the game knows about them.
Cards carry price information separately from the card itself, which is why price labels and a price-check screen exist.
What this entry does not tell you: the drop rate of any rarity or a price list. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A card is a physical object with its own display settings.
Rarity is a fixed set of levels.
Rarity is chosen in a dedicated screen.
Card prices are handled separately from the cards.
A card's record carries a border type, a grade and flags for being foil, for being a champion card and for being new.
facts.evidence: identifiers: CardData, borderType, isFoil, isChampionCard, isNew, cardGrade

facts.claim: The build ships the artwork behind a card border, including its inner mask and a glow, plus a group for the new-card marker.

The rarity and foil side is named piece by piece: a rarity image and text, a foil mask, a rainbow foil, rows for force foil, full-art foil, forced grade and grade collect, and separate foil and no-foil texts.
